extracted.intended_audience: anatomists, physicians, experimental natural philosophers, and practitioners of physiological/experimental medicine
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed, evidence-based reporting of anatomical and physiological experiments and observations (dissections, transfusions, magnetism, mining observations), aimed at supporting or refuting competing theories by empirical demonstration and procedural description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate anatomical function by ligature and dissection
rubrics_metrics.description: Evinced by ligatures, that the pretended vessels are neither those that are described by Bartholin ... nor others presumed to be known by Everhard alone; he proves that that duct goes to the receptacle, and there deposits its liquor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ligatures to trace vessels and show direction of flow; combine with accurate dissection across relevant organs to demonstrate whether a vessel conveys material to or from a given organ rather than relying on appearance or isolated reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use direct experimental disruption to reveal physiological pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: Dr. Lower, using to open sometimes the right side of the thorax, and with his fingers to break the receptacle ... dogs, well fed all the while, have thrown out all the chyle into the opened part of the thorax ... and were starved within three days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform controlled surgical or physical interventions (e.g., opening cavities, severing ducts) to observe consequences (e.g., loss of chyle, starvation) that prove where fluids go or are deposited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ comparative anatomy across species to test claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Dissect with all possible accuracy not only some of the larger animals, as cows and mares, but some of the smaller kind also, such as rabbits ... he examines ... and compares ... the variety of these phaenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test anatomical hypotheses across multiple species (large and small, oviparous and viviparous) to determine generality and to spot species-specific differences that bear on function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer precise morphological description, measurements, and illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: He annexes a particular description of the placenta of a woman ... The shape of that in a woman is orbicular, about a foot large, and two inches thick ... the whole is illustrated by many accurate engravings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give exact shapes, dimensions, distribution of vessels/fibres, and provide accurate illustrations to make observations verifiable and useful to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with competing theories and refute by evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Here are examined three opinions of Curvey, Everhard and Harvey ... This our author undertakes to disprove ... he defends the Harveian doctrine ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the rival hypotheses from prior authorities and present experiments or observations designed to support or refute each, rather than asserting conclusions without comparative analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infer function from patterns of anastomoses and vascular arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: He takes notice of the multitude of anastomoses, remarkable in the womb of pregnant creatures ... and subjoins a discussion of the way how the alimentary juice is in the womb severed from the mass of the blood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the presence, number and distribution of anastomoses and vessel networks to reason about how nourishment is delivered, transformed, or partitioned within an organ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze humours and membranes by physical-chemical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: These humours, he says, he has examined, by concreting, distilling, and coagulating them; where he furnishes the reader with no vulgar observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply preparative and analytical techniques (concreting, distillation, coagulation) to characterise embryonic humours and to distinguish nutritive from non-nutritive fluids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use behavioral and circumstantial evidence to infer internal states
rubrics_metrics.description: He proves air in the said membranes from the crying of infants in the womb ... and from chickens often heard to pip in the egg both before the breaking of the shells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correlate observable behaviors (in utero cries, egg pipping) and reported cases with anatomical/physiological inferences (presence of air, fermentation) to support claims about internal conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide procedural directions and checklists for dissectors
rubrics_metrics.description: The seventh and last chapter contains a direction for the younger anatomists, of what is to be observed in the dissection of divers animals with young: and first, of what is common ... then, what is peculiar ... lastly, what is observable in an eel, skate, salmon, frog, &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer species-specific procedural guidance (what to observe, how to sever structures conveniently, and what differences to expect) so novices can reproduce and assess findings reliably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer partial over total transfusion; practice circumspection for human application
rubrics_metrics.description: No considerate person, he observes, will venture upon a total transfusion, though he thinks a partial one may be serviceable in some cases ... it requires to be practised with much circumspection, otherwise it may be productive of mischief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When translating animal transfusion to human medicine, adopt conservative approaches (partial transfusion), carefully weigh risks and moral/legal considerations, and avoid reckless full-volume transfusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select appropriate subjects; avoid transfusing unsuitable patients
rubrics_metrics.description: The success of a larger transfusion ... he ascribes to the healthy and robust constitution of the individual ... Baron Bond ... died soon after the second operation. His disease was a mortification of the intestines, and he is thought to have been an unfit subject for the experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess patient suitability (overall health, comorbid pathology) before transfusion; frail or diseased organs may render the procedure dangerous or futile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use instrumented, replicable surgical technique for transfusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The instruments ... are only a silver tube, with a silver stopper somewhat blunted at one end ... After the artery is prepared in the lamb ... let a ligature be made upon the arm ... divide the skin ... open the vein ... insert the blunt-ended tube upwards into the vein ... pull out the stopper, and insert the pipe by which the arterial blood is to be infused ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe and standardize instruments and step-by-step surgical technique (ligature to engorge vein, skin incision, vein opening, tube insertion direction, assistant to compress vein) so operations can be performed consistently and evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use controls and alternative sources to identify causal effects (arterial vs venous)
rubrics_metrics.description: The experiment was repeated ... with this difference, that the blood was conducted through the tube from the jugular vein of the sheep, instead of an artery. The result was ... the animal was perfectly composed during the operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vary the source/type of transfused blood (arterial vs venous) to test mechanistic hypotheses (e.g., that oxygenated arterial blood entering the right heart produces fever); include direct comparisons to isolate causal factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record dose–response and correlate quantity transfused with severity
rubrics_metrics.description: The feverish symptoms were observed to be more or less violent in proportion to the quantity of arterial blood introduced into the vein of the recipient animal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically vary transfused volume and record clinical responses to establish dose–response relationships and identify safe/threshold doses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make objective quantitative measurements and clinical endpoint observations
rubrics_metrics.description: He drew three great dishes of blood from the dog ... weighed the other dog ... found his weight less by two pounds ... the recipient dog ... died five days after ... In other experiments: shivering, fever, thirst, convulsions, vomiting, appetite loss, and subsequent recovery were recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh subjects before and after procedures to quantify blood transferred; document objective clinical signs (temperature changes, convulsions, evacuations, survival) and time course of symptoms and recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate therapeutic utility by resuscitation experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: All the blood of a pointer was let out ... the blood was then transfused ... in less than half a minute after the introduction of the tube, he began to respire ... he leaped from the table and walked home, without experiencing any apparent inconvenience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test transfusion as a rescue therapy in extreme blood loss models; demonstrate rapid restoration of respiration and consciousness as clinically relevant outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test for transmissibility of disease or medicines via transfused blood
rubrics_metrics.description: Professor Harwood is at present engaged in a course of experiments to ascertain whether diseases may be communicated, or medicines conveyed into the system, by the transfusion of diseased or medicated blood from one animal to another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design follow-up experiments to assess whether pathological agents or pharmacologic effects transfer between donor and recipient, and report findings to guide safety evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replicate experiments broadly and across species to assess generality
rubrics_metrics.description: This experiment was performed before a very crowded meeting ... It has been frequently repeated since, and a variety of other animals have been subjected to the same experiments, and with equal success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat key experiments multiple times and in different species; report reproducibility and interspecies differences to establish robustness of conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document procedural and processing protocols for applied crafts (mining/ore processing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ore is beaten small; then washed clean in a running stream; then sifted ... the hearth or furnace is made of clay or fire-stone ... they throw the lead ore upon the wood, which melts down into the furnace; then with an iron ladle they take it out, cast it upon sand, and into what form they please.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide stepwise descriptions of processing (crushing, washing, sifting, furnace construction, fuel used, melting and casting) so that practices can be evaluated and reproduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record environmental and occupational health observations
rubrics_metrics.description: The natives and inhabitants are healthy ... except such as are employed in melting the lead at the mines; who, if they work in the smoak, are subject to a disease that kills them, and the cattle likewise that feed thereabouts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note local health hazards linked to industrial processes (smoke from lead melting) and effects on humans and livestock; such observations inform risk assessment and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geological field observations must be recorded but surface signs may be unreliable
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no certain signs above ground that afford any probability of a mine to my knowledge. The ore lies in veins as a wall; and is perfect lead, only on the outside covered with reddish earth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record macroscale landscape features (ridgelines, soil, stone types) and ore disposition, but caution that visible surface signs may not reliably indicate subsurface deposits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare precise instruments and control for artefacts in magnet experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: I caused a magnet to be turned with the powder of emery of a spherical form ... which ... had its three centres of magnitude, gravity, and magnetism all the same ... I caused two small holes to be made therein, to support it by two points of needles, as by two pivots ... put in a meridian of brass, and suspended the ball ... it was so easily moveable ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacture instruments with careful control (spherical form, coincident centers of gravity/magnetism), mount on pivots and a meridian standard, and eliminate gravity or balance artefacts so needle/ball movements reflect magnetic properties alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure magnetic declination at multiple meridian lines and report precisely
rubrics_metrics.description: I made that of the needle's declination on three different meridian lines, which I traced ... and found that the needle declined 44 degr. north-east.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform declination measurements at several meridians to test geographic variation; report angular measurements precisely and compare with prior observers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share observations and compare with prior authorities for community validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing can be more agreeable to me than to discourse on this subject, especially with the philosophers of England ... so that it is just that the observations made elsewhere concerning the same should return thither as to its source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate results to the scholarly community, reference earlier work (e.g., Gilbert), and invite comparative assessment to build consensus and correct errors.
